sourcedFrom: PSA AK FAMILY OWNERS MANUAL — 0626 — from the document's filename only; no part, form or revision code is printed in the book (not printed in the book)
cleanIntro:
This guide follows Palmetto State Armory's manual for its AK family, which does not name the PSAK GF3, so check your variant against it. PSA states that the overall function and disassembly instructions remain the same across the AK styles the book covers; every step below is quoted from that book and stated as generally as the book states it.

The strip is the classic AK sequence: magazine rocked out, dust cover off rear end first, driving spring forward and out, carrier fully back and up, bolt twisted free, then the gas tube and upper handguard off on their lock. PSA says no further disassembly is needed for cleaning, and the guide stops there. On this pattern the carrier does NOT lock open after the last round — the book prints the hold-open for the AKV and AK 556 only — so checking the chamber means holding the charging handle back yourself.

steps.title: ⛔ SAFE up, magazine ROCKED out, handle held back, chamber checked
steps.action: This guide follows Palmetto State Armory's manual for its AK family, which does not name the PSAK GF3, so check your variant against it. Muzzle in a safe direction, finger off the trigger. Push the safety selector all the way up to SAFE. Press the magazine release catch with your thumb, pivot the rear of the magazine forward until the front latch clears, and pull it down. Then pull the charging handle back, hold it there, and look through the ejection port into the chamber.
steps.prose: Hold it back by hand — this pattern has no hold-open, and a handle you let go of closes the chamber you were about to look at.
steps.aside: Look into the receiver through the ejection port and verify that there are no cartridges in the chamber
steps.quote: Press the magazine release catch with your thumb (1.) and pivot the rear of the magazine until the front latch is clear (2.), then pull the magazine down to remove.
steps.cite: PSA AK FAMILY OWNERS MANUAL — 0626 — from the document's filename only; no part, form or revision code is printed in the book — Unloading the firearm, step 2, printed p.17

steps.title: Dust cover: press the driving spring guide IN, lift the cover REAR END FIRST
steps.action: Press the serrated end of the driving spring guide into the dust cover and hold it in. With it held, lift the cover away rear end first. The guide is what retains the cover; if the cover will not lift, the guide is not far enough in.
steps.prose: Rear end first, every time. Levering the front first bends the lip that locates the cover.
steps.caution: NOTICE: Your firearm may differ slightly from the images shown; however, the overall function and disassembly instructions will remain the same.
steps.quote: Press the serrated end of the driving spring guide (A.) into the bolt cover, and while holding the guide in, lift off the bolt cover, rear end first.
steps.cite: PSA AK FAMILY OWNERS MANUAL — 0626 — from the document's filename only; no part, form or revision code is printed in the book — Disassembly, step 2, printed p.23

steps.title: Driving spring assembly: push FORWARD to unseat, then draw it out
steps.action: Push forward on the end of the driving spring guide to disengage it from its seat in the rear of the receiver, then pull the complete driving spring assembly out of the bolt carrier. It is under compression — keep a hand on it as it comes free.
steps.prose: Forward to unseat, not up. The seat only releases along the axis of the spring.
steps.quote: Push forward on the end of the driving spring guide, disengaging it from it’s seat in the rear of the receiver.
steps.cite: PSA AK FAMILY OWNERS MANUAL — 0626 — from the document's filename only; no part, form or revision code is printed in the book — Disassembly, step 3, printed p.23

steps.title: Bolt carrier: fully to the REAR, lift slightly, out the back
steps.action: Pull the operating handle and bolt carrier fully to the rear, lift the carrier slightly upward, and remove the bolt and carrier together by pulling them to the rear.
steps.prose: If it will not lift, it is not far enough back. Nothing about this step rewards force.
steps.quote: Pull the operating handle and bolt carrier (B.) fully to the rear, lift the bolt carrier slightly upward, and then remove the bolt and carrier (B.) by pulling it to the rear
steps.cite: PSA AK FAMILY OWNERS MANUAL — 0626 — from the document's filename only; no part, form or revision code is printed in the book — Disassembly, step 4, printed p.24

steps.title: Bolt out of the carrier: press IN, twist the lug clear of its cam path
steps.action: Press the bolt into the carrier until its operating lug can be twisted free of the cam path, then pull the bolt straight forward and out. The lug rides that cam path to rotate the bolt when the rifle fires; you are walking it out of the same track by hand.
steps.prose: Press first, then twist. Twisting against the cam without pressing in is how the lug gets burred.
steps.quote: Press the bolt into the carrier until the bolt operating lug can be twisted free of its cam path in the carrier [Figure 19]. Pull the bolt straight forward and out of the carrier.
steps.cite: PSA AK FAMILY OWNERS MANUAL — 0626 — from the document's filename only; no part, form or revision code is printed in the book — Disassembly, step 5, printed p.24

steps.title: Gas tube and upper handguard: rotate the LOCK up, lift the rear, slide REARWARD
steps.action: Rotate the gas cylinder tube lock upward to free the upper handguard and gas tube. Pull up on the REAR of the handguard to take it off, then lift the rear of the gas tube and slide it rearward to clear the gas block.
steps.prose: The lock is a stiff cam and wants a firm thumb. It should rotate, not bend.
steps.quote: Rotate the gas cylinder tube lock upward (C.) to free the upper hand guard and gas cylinder tube.
steps.cite: PSA AK FAMILY OWNERS MANUAL — 0626 — from the document's filename only; no part, form or revision code is printed in the book — Disassembly, step 6, printed p.24

steps.title: Field strip complete — PSA says stop here
steps.action: Dust cover, driving spring assembly, bolt carrier, bolt, gas tube and upper handguard. PSA states plainly that no further disassembly is needed for cleaning, and that is the line to hold: the trigger group and the barrel assembly are not part of an owner's clean.
steps.prose: A maker who tells you where to stop has done you a favour.
steps.quote: No further disassembly is needed for cleaning.
steps.cite: PSA AK FAMILY OWNERS MANUAL — 0626 — from the document's filename only; no part, form or revision code is printed in the book — Disassembly, printed p.24

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Inside the carrier stays DRY
deepSteps.action: Clean the bolt carrier group with CLP or a suitable solvent, then take the excess oil back off the bolt assembly before it goes together. PSA wants the inside of the carrier dry and only the exterior lubricated.
deepSteps.prose: Oil inside the carrier collects carbon and turns to grinding paste.
deepSteps.quote: Be sure to remove excess oil from the bolt assembly before reassembly, do not lubricate the inside of the carrier. Lubricate the exterior of the carrier only.
deepSteps.cite: PSA AK FAMILY OWNERS MANUAL — 0626 — from the document's filename only; no part, form or revision code is printed in the book — Cleaning the bolt carrier group, printed p.28

deepSteps.title: Chamber: patch until clean, then DRY — no oil
deepSteps.action: Scrub the chamber with a chamber brush and solvent, patch it until a patch stays clean, then run a dry patch and leave it dry.
deepSteps.prose: The one place on the gun where 'a little oil to protect it' is wrong.
deepSteps.quote: Clean the chamber with a chamber cleaning brush, and a bore solvent or CLP. Move the brush through the chamber several times to scrub the inside of the chamber. Use a clean patch to wipe the chamber after cleaning. Repeat with clean patches until patch stays clean. After cleaning, run a dry patch through the chamber. Do not oil the chamber.
deepSteps.cite: PSA AK FAMILY OWNERS MANUAL — 0626 — from the document's filename only; no part, form or revision code is printed in the book — Cleaning the chamber, printed p.27

deepSteps.title: Bore from the chamber end, and mind the rod
deepSteps.action: Run the rod from the chamber end so fouling leaves at the muzzle. Keep the rod off the bore and chamber walls — PSA warns against letting the rod scratch either.
deepSteps.prose: A bore guide costs less than a barrel.
deepSteps.aside: Do not allow cleaning rods to scratch the inside of the barrel or chamber.
deepSteps.quote: Using a cleaning rod, pass a patch soaked in bore cleaner through the barrel several times starting from the chamber end.
deepSteps.cite: PSA AK FAMILY OWNERS MANUAL — 0626 — from the document's filename only; no part, form or revision code is printed in the book — Cleaning the barrel, printed p.27

deepSteps.title: Solvent choice is a maintenance decision
deepSteps.action: Use a cleaning solution made for firearms. PSA warns in its own notice that some solutions and solvents will damage the gun.
deepSteps.prose: The finish is the corrosion protection. Stripping it is not cleaning.
deepSteps.quote: Some cleaning solutions and solvents may damage your firearm. Use a cleaning solution that is designed for use on firearms.
deepSteps.cite: PSA AK FAMILY OWNERS MANUAL — 0626 — from the document's filename only; no part, form or revision code is printed in the book — Maintenance, printed p.27

cleaning.name: CHAMBER
tasks: Verify unloaded and the safety on SAFE before anything else.
Scrub with a chamber brush and bore solvent or CLP, several passes.
Patch until a patch stays clean, then run a DRY patch through.
⛔ Do not oil the chamber — PSA says so explicitly.

cleaning.name: BARREL AND BORE
tasks: Patch soaked in bore cleaner from the CHAMBER end, several passes.
Brush with more bore cleaner to lift copper fouling and powder residue.
Patch again until a clean patch exits, then a patch coated in gun oil to finish.
Outside of the barrel: nylon brush and cleaner-lubricant, then wipe clean.

cleaning.name: BOLT CARRIER GROUP
tasks: Clean with CLP or a suitable solvent.
⛔ Remove excess oil from the bolt assembly before reassembly and do NOT lubricate the inside of the carrier — exterior only.

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Wipe all metal with a clean cloth, then follow with a lightly oiled cloth.

reassembly: Gas tube forward into the gas block, upper handguard on, then rotate the lock DOWN to capture both.
Bolt into the carrier: enter it straight, then twist the operating lug back into its cam path.
Carrier and bolt into the receiver at the rear, then run it forward onto the rails.
Driving spring assembly into the carrier, then push FORWARD and drop the guide into its seat in the rear of the receiver.
Dust cover FRONT edge located first, then press the rear down until the driving spring guide snaps through.
⛔ Function-check before the rifle goes away.
fncheck: With the rifle CLEAR and the safety worked through its positions, cycle the charging handle several times and watch the carrier return fully forward under spring pressure alone. Confirm the dust cover is captured and does not lift at the rear. Rock an EMPTY magazine in front lip first and confirm it locks with a click, then rock it back out. On this pattern the carrier closes on an empty magazine rather than locking open — that is normal per PSA's book, not a fault.
